title: Proverbs, Chapter 21 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 21 on folios 416v, 417r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 21 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 416v, 417r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>פַּלְגֵי־מַ֣יִם לֶב־מֶ֭לֶךְ בְּיַד־יְהוָ֑ה עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יַחְפֹּ֣ץ יַטֶּֽנּוּ׃ <sup>2</sup>כָּֽל־דֶּרֶךְ־אִ֭ישׁ יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃ <sup>3</sup>עֲ֭שֹׂה צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נִבְחָ֖ר לַיהוָ֣ה מִזָּֽבַח׃ <sup>4</sup>רוּם־עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַב־לֵ֑ב נִ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃ <sup>5</sup>מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת חָ֭רוּץ אַךְ־לְמוֹתָ֑ר וְכָל־אָ֝֗ץ אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃ <sup>6</sup>פֹּ֣עַל א֭וֹצָרוֹת בִּלְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר הֶ֥בֶל נִ֝דָּ֗ף מְבַקְשֵׁי־מָֽוֶת׃ <sup>7</sup>שֹׁד־רְשָׁעִ֥ים יְגוֹרֵ֑ם כִּ֥י מֵ֝אֲנ֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃ <sup>8</sup>הֲפַכְפַּ֬ךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ וָזָ֑ר וְ֝זַ֗ךְ יָשָׁ֥ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will. <sup>2</sup>Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts. <sup>3</sup>To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice. <sup>4</sup>An high look, and a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked, is sin. <sup>5</sup>The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want. <sup>6</sup>The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death. <sup>7</sup>The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment. <sup>8</sup>The way of man is froward and strange: but as for the pure, his work is right.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>ט֗וֹב לָשֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃ <sup>10</sup>נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָ֭שָׁע אִוְּתָה־רָ֑ע לֹא־יֻחַ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֣יו רֵעֵֽהוּ׃ <sup>11</sup>בַּעְנָשׁ־לֵ֭ץ יֶחְכַּם־פֶּ֑תִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְ֝חָכָ֗ם יִקַּח־דָּֽעַת׃ <sup>12</sup>מַשְׂכִּ֣יל צַ֭דִּיק לְבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע מְסַלֵּ֖ף רְשָׁעִ֣ים לָרָֽע׃ <sup>13</sup>אֹטֵ֣ם אָ֭זְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל גַּֽם־ה֥וּא יִ֝קְרָ֗א וְלֹ֣א יֵעָנֶֽה׃ <sup>14</sup>מַתָּ֣ן בַּ֭סֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה־אָ֑ף וְשֹׁ֥חַד בַּ֝חֵ֗ק חֵמָ֥ה עַזָּֽה׃ <sup>15</sup>שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַ֭צַּדִּיק עֲשׂ֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃ <sup>16</sup>אָדָ֗ם תּ֖וֹעֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house. <sup>10</sup>The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes. <sup>11</sup>When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge. <sup>12</sup>The righteous man wisely considereth the house of the wicked: but God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness. <sup>13</sup>Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard. <sup>14</sup>A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath. <sup>15</sup>It is joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity. <sup>16</sup>The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>אִ֣ישׁ מַ֭חְסוֹר אֹהֵ֣ב שִׂמְחָ֑ה אֹהֵ֥ב יַֽיִן־וָ֝שֶׁ֗מֶן לֹ֣א יַעֲשִֽׁיר׃ <sup>18</sup>כֹּ֣פֶר לַצַּדִּ֣יק רָשָׁ֑ע וְתַ֖חַת יְשָׁרִ֣ים בּוֹגֵֽד׃ <sup>19</sup>ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִדְבָּ֑ר מֵאֵ֖שֶׁת מדונים [מִדְיָנִ֣ים] וָכָֽעַס׃ <sup>20</sup>אוֹצָ֤ר ׀ נֶחְמָ֣ד וָ֭שֶׁמֶן בִּנְוֵ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וּכְסִ֖יל אָדָ֣ם יְבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>21</sup>רֹ֭דֵף צְדָקָ֣ה וָחָ֑סֶד יִמְצָ֥א חַ֝יִּ֗ים צְדָקָ֥ה וְכָבֽוֹד׃ <sup>22</sup>עִ֣יר גִּ֭בֹּרִים עָלָ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗רֶד עֹ֣ז מִבְטֶחָֽה׃ <sup>23</sup>שֹׁמֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו וּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֖ר מִצָּר֣וֹת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃ <sup>24</sup>זֵ֣ד יָ֭הִיר לֵ֣ץ שְׁמ֑וֹ ע֝וֹשֶׂ֗ה בְּעֶבְרַ֥ת זָדֽוֹן׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich. <sup>18</sup>The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright. <sup>19</sup>It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman. <sup>20</sup>There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up. <sup>21</sup>He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour. <sup>22</sup>A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof. <sup>23</sup>Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles. <sup>24</sup>Proud and haughty scorner is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>תַּאֲוַ֣ת עָצֵ֣ל תְּמִיתֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־מֵאֲנ֖וּ יָדָ֣יו לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃ <sup>26</sup>כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם הִתְאַוָּ֣ה תַאֲוָ֑ה וְצַדִּ֥יק יִ֝תֵּ֗ן וְלֹ֣א יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃ <sup>27</sup>זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָ֑ה אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־בְזִמָּ֥ה יְבִיאֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>28</sup>עֵד־כְּזָבִ֥ים יֹאבֵ֑ד וְאִ֥ישׁ שׁ֝וֹמֵ֗עַ לָנֶ֥צַח יְדַבֵּֽר׃ <sup>29</sup>הֵעֵ֬ז אִ֣ישׁ רָשָׁ֣ע בְּפָנָ֑יו וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר ה֤וּא ׀ יכין [יָבִ֬ין] דרכיו [דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃] <sup>30</sup>אֵ֣ין חָ֭כְמָה וְאֵ֣ין תְּבוּנָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין עֵ֝צָ֗ה לְנֶ֣גֶד יְהוָֽה׃ פ <sup>31</sup>ס֗וּס מ֭וּכָן לְי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְ֝לַֽיהוָ֗ה הַתְּשׁוּעָֽה׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour. <sup>26</sup>He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not. <sup>27</sup>The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind? <sup>28</sup>A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly. <sup>29</sup>A wicked man hardeneth his face: but as for the upright, he directeth his way. <sup>30</sup>There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD. <sup>31</sup>The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD.
